316244.title: Conjecture on fixed-length complete sums in cyclic groups
316244.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $A\subset\mathbb Z_n$ be a set whose elements are all coprime to $n$. For a positive integer $k$, let $k\wedge A$ denote the set of sums of $k$ distinct elements of $A$.

**Fixed-length complete-sums conjecture.** If

$$
|A|\geq\sqrt{4n-4},
$$

then

$$
|k\wedge A|=n,
$$

where $k=\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$.

This is presented as a conjecture following the paper's main theorem and is not stated as proved; its status is therefore open.
316244.source_name: Y. O. Hamidoune, A. S. Lladó and O. Serra, “On complete subsets of the cyclic group”, arXiv:0704.0541 (2007).
316244.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.0541

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2007). “This conjecture was proved by Olson.”

316327.title: The geometric realization conjecture for triangulated closed orientable surfaces of genus at most four
316327.statement:
A **triangulation** is a simplicial decomposition of a closed orientable surface. A triangulation is **realizable in** $\mathbb{R}^3$ when its vertices can be embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$ so that its edges are straight, its triangles are flat, and distinct simplices do not intersect except along shared faces.

**Geometric realization conjecture.** Every triangulation of a closed orientable surface of genus at most $4$ is realizable in $\mathbb{R}^3$ by straight edges, flat triangles, and without self-intersections.

The conjecture is true for spheres, but its natural extension to closed orientable surfaces of greater genus is false. The stated genus-at-most-four claim is therefore resolved as part of the known geometric realization results for triangulated surfaces.
316327.source_name: Gennaro Amendola, “Decomposition and Enumeration of Triangulated Surfaces”, arXiv:0705.1835 (2007).
316327.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.1835

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2007).

316484.title: Dynnikov–Wiest conjecture on linear-length sigma-consistent braid representatives
316484.statement: Let $B_n$ be the braid group with generating set $\Sigma=\{\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_{n-1}\}$, and let $l_\Sigma(w)$ denote the $\Sigma$-length of a braid $w$. A braid word is **$\sigma$-consistent** if it is trivial, $\sigma$-positive, or $\sigma$-negative, where these notions are defined using the standard generators and their inverses. **Dynnikov–Wiest conjecture.** There are numbers $\lambda,c$ such that every braid $w\in B_n$ has a $\sigma$-consistent representative whose $\Sigma$-length is bounded linearly by the $\Sigma$-length of $w$; that is, the representative has length at most $\lambda l_\Sigma(w)+c$. The conjecture concerns whether the currently known exponential bound for such representatives can be replaced by a linear one. Its resolution is not supplied in the paper.
316484.source_name: Alexei G. Myasnikov and Alexander Ushakov, “Random subgroups and analysis of the length-based and quotient attacks”, arXiv:0707.1501 (2007).
316484.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.1501

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2007).

316616.title: The missing-face embeddability conjecture for triangulated spheres
316616.statement:
Let $\mathsf{S}_{\leq d}$ be the $d$-skeleton of a triangulated $2d$-sphere and let $M$ be a **missing** $d$-face of $\mathsf{S}_{\leq d}$. Then $\mathsf{K}:=\mathsf{S}_{\leq d}\cup\{M\}$ is the resulting complex.

**Missing-face embeddability conjecture.** The complex $\mathsf{K}$ does not embed in the $2d$-sphere.

The theorem preceding this conjecture establishes the same assertion for piecewise linear spheres. The conjecture claims that the piecewise-linearity hypothesis is unnecessary.
316616.source_name: Eran Nevo and Uli Wagner, “On the Embeddability of Skeleta of Spheres”, arXiv:0709.0988 (2007).
316616.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.0988

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

316626.title: Birkhoff-polytope uniqueness conjecture for permutation groups
316626.statement:
Let $G$ be a permutation group and let $P(G)$ denote its permutation polytope. Let $B_n$ be the Birkhoff polytope.

**Birkhoff-polytope uniqueness conjecture.** If $P(G)$ is combinatorially equivalent to $B_n$ for some $n$, then $G$ is effectively equivalent to $S_n$.

The observation motivating the claim is that $B_3$ is realized by the full symmetric group $S_3$, which appears to be essentially the only such permutation group in that case. The general statement remains open.
316626.source_name: Barbara Baumeister, Christian Haase, Benjamin Nill and Andreas Paffenholz, “On permutation polytopes”, arXiv:0709.1615 (2007).
316626.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

316627.title: Affine-automorphism conjecture for abelian permutation groups
316627.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian permutation group, let $P(G)$ be its permutation polytope, and write $|G|$ for the order of $G$.

**Affine-automorphism conjecture.** If

$$
|G|>2,
$$

then the group of affine automorphisms of $P(G)$ contains more elements than $G$.

For nonabelian groups, left and right multiplication already provide the motivating source of additional affine automorphisms. The assertion for abelian groups of order greater than two is presented as open.
316627.source_name: Barbara Baumeister, Christian Haase, Benjamin Nill and Andreas Paffenholz, “On permutation polytopes”, arXiv:0709.1615 (2007).
316627.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

316628.title: Free-sum conjecture for centrally symmetric faces of permutation polytopes
316628.statement:
Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be centrally symmetric faces of permutation polytopes, and let their free sum denote the corresponding polyhedral free-sum construction.

**Free-sum conjecture.** The free sum of centrally symmetric faces of permutation polytopes can be combinatorially realized as a face of a permutation polytope.

The claim is motivated by constructions showing that bipyramids over centrally symmetric faces should again be realizable as faces. The paper presents the broader free-sum realization claim without a resolution.
316628.source_name: Barbara Baumeister, Christian Haase, Benjamin Nill and Andreas Paffenholz, “On permutation polytopes”, arXiv:0709.1615 (2007).
316628.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

316629.title: Wedge conjecture for faces of permutation polytopes
316629.statement:
Let $F$ be a face of a permutation polytope and let $F'$ be a face of $F$. The wedge over $F'$ is the polyhedral construction described in the paper, and the complement of $F'$ in $F$ is considered as a face condition.

**Wedge conjecture.** The wedge over $F'$ can be combinatorially realized as a face of a permutation polytope if, or only if, the complement of $F'$ in $F$ is a face of $F$.

The conjecture is based on explicit checks in low dimensions and proposes a necessary-and-sufficient criterion for wedge realizability. Its general validity remains open.
316629.source_name: Barbara Baumeister, Christian Haase, Benjamin Nill and Andreas Paffenholz, “On permutation polytopes”, arXiv:0709.1615 (2007).
316629.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

316665.title: The nice perfect-elimination characterization of graph polynomials
316665.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $R_G(q)$ be the polynomial associated with $G$. A **nice perfect elimination order** is the graph-theoretic ordering defined in the surrounding work, and a product of $q$-numbers means a factorization into such factors.

**Nice perfect-elimination conjecture.** The polynomial $R_G(q)$ can be factorized as a product of $q$-numbers if and only if the graph $G$ has a nice perfect elimination order.

This is presented as a possible converse to a preceding corollary, relating a factorization property of $R_G(q)$ to a structural elimination ordering of $G$. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
316665.source_name: Suho Oh, Alexander Postnikov and Hwanchul Yoo, “Bruhat order, smooth Schubert varieties, and hyperplane arrangements”, arXiv:0709.3259 (2007).
316665.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.3259

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

316668.title: The Colin de Verdière stress-freeness conjecture
316668.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mu(G)$ denote the Colin de Verdière parameter of $G$. A graph is generically $k$-stress free when its generic $k$-dimensional rigidity stress space is trivial.

**Colin de Verdière stress-freeness conjecture.** If $\mu(G)\leq k$ for a positive integer $k$, then $G$ is generically $k$-stress free.

This would extend the known implications for planar and linklessly embeddable graphs, corresponding to $\mu(G)\leq 3$ and $\mu(G)\leq 4$. The source presents the general statement as open.
316668.source_name: Eran Nevo, “Algebraic Shifting and f-Vector Theory”, arXiv:0709.3265 (2007).
316668.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.3265

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

316858.title: Orbit representatives conjecture for short roots of type C
316858.statement:
Let $\Delta$ be of type $C_n$, let $\Delta_s^+(C_n)$ be its short positive roots, and let $\mathfrak X_s$ be the reverse operator on their antichains. Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$ be the standard simple roots. **Orbit representatives conjecture.** Every $\mathfrak X_s$-orbit has cardinality

$$
2n-1=h^*(B_n),
$$

and each orbit contains a unique antichain contained in

$$
\Delta^+(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_{n-2})\simeq\Delta^+(A_{n-2}).
$$

The source presents this as a more precise conjecture for type $C_n$ after noting the isomorphism with the corresponding poset above the simple roots; no general resolution is supplied.
316858.source_name: Dmitri I. Panyushev, “On orbits of antichains of positive roots”, arXiv:0711.3353 (2008).
316858.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.3353

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2007).

316908.title: Sufficiency of the NR-facet condition for parsimonious relaxations
316908.statement: Let $P_n$ be the Graphical Traveling Salesman Polyhedron, let $mathcal G_B$ be the graph associated with a relaxation $mathcal R_B$, and call a facet of $P_n$ an NR-facet when it has the stated non-rank property. **Parsimonious-relaxation conjecture.** If every connected component of $mathcal G_B$ contains a vertex corresponding to an NR-facet of $P_n$, then the relaxation $mathcal R_B$ has the parsimonious property. This conjectures that the necessary condition established in the cited theorem is also sufficient; the supplied text gives no resolution.
316908.source_name: Dirk Oliver Theis, “On the facial structure of Symmetric and Graphical Traveling Salesman Polyhedra”, arXiv:0712.1269 (2009).
316908.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.1269

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2007).

318077.title: Tucker's perfect-graph sequential colorability conjecture
318077.statement:
Let $\mathrm{G}$ be a perfect graph, and let $t$ be the relevant coloring parameter. The graph is **uniquely $t$-colorable** when it has a unique partition into $t$ color classes, while it is **sequentially $t$-colorable** when its vertices can be ordered so that, starting from a $t$-clique with distinct colors, each subsequent vertex receives a forced color by Tucker's sequential coloring rules.

**Tucker's conjecture.** For perfect graphs, unique $t$-colorability is equivalent to sequential $t$-colorability.

The equivalence is known in the supplied text for comparability graphs, complements of comparability graphs, chordal graphs, and complements of chordal graphs. The extension to all perfect graphs is presented as a conjecture, and no resolution is given here.
318077.source_name: Amir Daneshgar and Roozbeh Ebrahimi Soorchaei, “On Sequential Coloring of Graphs and its Defining Sets”, arXiv:0812.4920 (2008).
318077.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.4920

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2008).

318786.title: The logarithmic multipermutation-level conjecture for square-free solutions
318786.statement:
Suppose $(X,r)$ is a nondegenerate square-free multipermutation solution of finite order $n$, and let $\mathop{\mathrm{mpl}}(X)$ denote its multipermutation level.

**Logarithmic multipermutation-level conjecture.** One has

$$
\mathop{\mathrm{mpl}}(X)<\log_2 n.
$$

This conjecture gives a logarithmic upper bound on the multipermutation level in terms of the order of the solution, refining the expectation that finite square-free solutions have controlled retraction complexity. The source attributes it to the more recent conjecture cited as T08ini; no resolution is stated in the supplied text.
318786.source_name: Tatiana Gateva-Ivanova and Peter Cameron, “Multipermutation solutions of the Yang–Baxter equation”, arXiv:0907.4276 (2009).
318786.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2009). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0806.2928](https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.2928).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.4276

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2009).

380326.title: Conjecture on the structure of a minimal configuration in Moser's worm problem
380326.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}$ be the fixed line segment, $\mathcal{S}$ the square, and let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the triangular objects in the configuration. Consider configurations with $y_1\geq 0$ and minimize the area of their convex hull. **Minimal-configuration conjecture.** The optimal configuration of $\mathcal{L}$, $\mathcal{T}$ and $\mathcal{T}$ must have the following properties: (1) the right-most vertex of $\mathcal{T}$ coincides with the point $(1,0)$ of $\mathcal{L}$; (2) the top-most vertices of $\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{T}$ coincide. The properties are suggested by numerical grid-search experiments in the study of lower bounds for Moser's worm problem; the supplied text gives no proof or resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
380326.source_name: Tirasan Khandhawit and Sira Sriswasdi, “An Improved Lower Bound for Moser's Worm Problem”, arXiv:math/0701391 (2009).
380326.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701391

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2007).

380333.title: The complementation-set correspondence conjecture
380333.statement: Let $G$ be a bicoloured graph with no isolated vertices and no twins, where twins are vertices having identical relevant neighbourhoods. Let $[G]$ denote the parity class of $G$, and let a **complementation set** be as defined in the paper. **Complementation-set correspondence conjecture.** The parity class $[G]$ is in bijection with the complementation sets of $G$. The supplied text gives no resolution status and does not provide the definitions needed to specify the bijection more explicitly.
380333.source_name: François Genest, “Eulerian graphs and local complementation”, arXiv:math/0701421 (2007).
380333.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701421

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2007).

380416.title: The algebraicity conjecture for hereditary ordered graph speeds
380416.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the set of exponential growth constants arising from hereditary properties of ordered graphs. Let $\mathbb{A}$ denote the set of algebraic numbers and $\mathbb{Q}$ the set of rational numbers.

**Algebraicity conjecture.** Every $c\in\mathcal{S}$ is either an integer or an irrational algebraic number; equivalently,

$$
\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}\cup(\mathbb{A}\setminus\mathbb{Q}).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the fact that all speeds found in the paper are integers or algebraic irrationals. The supplied text gives no resolution.
380416.source_name: József Balogh, Béla Bollobás and Robert Morris, “Hereditary properties of ordered graphs”, arXiv:math/0702352 (2007).
380416.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0702352

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2007). “We shall discuss these and other open questions in greater length in Section , but let us now return to the proof of Theorem .”

380453.title: The exchange-graph conjecture for cluster algebras
380453.statement: Let ${\mathcal A}$ be a cluster algebra with initial exchange matrix $B$. Its exchange graph is the quotient of the regular tree of seeds by simultaneous permutations of cluster variables, coefficients, and the rows and columns of the exchange matrix. **Exchange-graph conjecture.** The exchange graph of a cluster algebra depends only on the initial exchange matrix $B$. This conjecture asserts that the exchange graph is independent of the chosen coefficients or realization of the cluster algebra, once $B$ is fixed. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
380453.source_name: Michael Gekhtman, Michael Shapiro and Alek Vainshtein, “On the properties of the exchange graph of a cluster algebra”, arXiv:math/0703151 (2015).
380453.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0703151

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2007).

380467.title: Shibuya's cobordism conjecture for self Delta-equivalence
380467.statement: Let oriented links be related by **self $\Delta$-equivalence** when one can be transformed into the other by self delta moves and ambient isotopies, where each self delta move has all three strings belonging to the same link component. Two oriented links are **cobordant** if they cobound disjoint unions of properly embedded surfaces in $S^3\times[0,1]$. **Shibuya's conjecture.** Any two cobordant oriented links are self $\Delta$-equivalent. This conjecture concerns the relationship between link cobordism and self Delta-equivalence; the source presents it as a conjecture, and no resolution is given in the supplied text.
380467.source_name: Ryo Nikkuni, “Delta edge-homotopy invariants of spatial graphs via disk-summing the constituent knots”, arXiv:math/0703319 (2007).
380467.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0703319

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2007).

381028.title: The inner-product formula for the patterns $J_{k,n}$
381028.statement:
Let $J_{k,n}\in\mathcal P'_n$, for $k\in\mathbb Z_{n-1}$, be the union of the translate $(0,1)+\mathrm{NE}_{n-1}$, the product $\{n\}\times\mathbb Z_k$, and the set $\{(i,1):k<i<n\}$. Then

**The $J_{k,n}$ inner-product conjecture.**

$$
\langle \chi_{J_{k,n}},\chi_n\rangle=(-1)^{n-1}\binom{n}{k}\binom{n-2}{k-1}.
$$

This formula is proposed in connection with the preceding theorem and gives an explicit value for the inner product of the characteristic polynomial of $J_{k,n}$ with the Vandermonde polynomial $\chi_n$. The supplied text gives no resolution status or supporting results beyond presenting it as a proposed statement.
381028.source_name: Jinpeng An and Dragomir Z. Djokovic, “Zero patterns and unitary similarity”, arXiv:0807.3580 (2009).
381028.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.3580

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2008).
